summary: Persistent Middle East maritime disruptions and energy price volatility are forcing Indian and Chinese trade corridors to shift from short-term cost hedging toward structural self-reliance. While China leverages managed currency adjustments, green bunkering dominance, and expanded logistics hubs to sustain its export momentum, India is countering potential Chinese supply restrictions by accelerating deepwater port integration, record warehousing expansion, and direct trade pacts like the EU FTA. Moving forward, continued chokepoint risks will drive increased captive fleet acquisitions by refiners and accelerate localized manufacturing across South Asia to bypass volatile ocean freight routes.
